paragraphs.title: Preparing for War and the First Prophecy

easy.explanation: The KJV says, “And they continued three years without war between Syria and Israel.”
easy.q: How long had there been no war between Syria and Israel?

easy.explanation: He said, “Know ye that Ramoth in Gilead is ours.”
easy.q: Which city did the king of Israel want to recover from Syria?

easy.explanation: Jehoshaphat said, “Enquire, I pray thee, at the word of the Lord to day.”
easy.q: Who asked that the word of the Lord be sought before going to battle?

answers: To ask whether to go to battle
medium.explanation: He asked whether he should go against Ramothgilead or forbear.
medium.q: Why did the king of Israel gather the prophets?

medium.explanation: They said, “Go up; for the Lord shall deliver it into the hand of the king.”
medium.q: What did the approximately four hundred prophets answer?

medium.explanation: The king questioned why they were still inactive instead of taking Ramothgilead.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “we be still” mean in this context?

answers: They all gave the same favorable message, but no prophet of the Lord had yet been consulted
They wanted to go without an army
They refused to speak to the king
challenge.explanation: Jehoshaphat asked whether there was another prophet of the Lord who could be consulted.
challenge.q: Why was Jehoshaphat suspicious of the prophets’ answer?

answers: He wanted to rely only on military strength
He wanted the decision tested by the word of the Lord
He opposed every alliance with Israel
challenge.explanation: Although he agreed to join the campaign, he insisted on hearing the word of the Lord.
challenge.q: What does Jehoshaphat’s request reveal about his approach to war?

answers: Micaiah foretold disaster, while the others foretold success
Micaiah spoke of peace, while the others spoke of surrender
Micaiah refused to speak, while the others remained silent
challenge.explanation: Micaiah foretold scattered Israel and disaster, while the other prophets promised victory.
challenge.q: What was the main difference between Micaiah’s prophecy and the other prophets’ message?

paragraphs.title: Micaiah’s Vision and the Lying Spirit

answers: The Lord sitting on His throne
easy.explanation: Micaiah said, “I saw the Lord sitting on his throne.”
easy.q: What did Micaiah see in his vision?

answers: Become a lying spirit in the mouths of all his prophets
easy.explanation: The spirit said, “I will be a lying spirit in the mouth of all his prophets.”
easy.q: What did the spirit propose to do to persuade Ahab?

answers: He smote him on the cheek
easy.explanation: The KJV says that Zedekiah “smote Micaiah on the cheek.”
easy.q: What did Zedekiah the son of Chenaanah do to Micaiah?

answers: A lying spirit was in their mouths
medium.explanation: Micaiah explained that the Lord had put a lying spirit in the mouths of Ahab’s prophets.
medium.q: Why did Micaiah say that Ahab’s prophets prophesied good?

answers: Israel would be without a leader and scattered
Israel would hide from the prophets
medium.explanation: The vision said they had no master and should return every man to his house.
medium.q: What did the vision of Israel scattered like sheep without a shepherd mean?

answers: Food and drink given in hardship and deprivation
medium.explanation: Ahab ordered Micaiah to be imprisoned and fed under difficult, deprived conditions.
medium.q: What does “bread of affliction and water of affliction” mean?

answers: It warned that Ahab would fall, but Ahab still went to battle
It promised that Ahab would return safely
It gave instructions only to Jehoshaphat
challenge.explanation: Micaiah described Israel scattered and Ahab falling, but Ahab proceeded to battle.
challenge.q: How did Micaiah’s vision relate to Ahab’s decision to fight?

answers: He gladly accepted the word of the Lord
He knew Micaiah always prophesied good concerning him
He rejected the prophecy because it was unwelcome
challenge.explanation: Ahab said that he hated Micaiah because he did not prophesy good concerning him, but evil.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from Ahab’s response to Micaiah’s prophecy?

answers: Ahab’s peaceful return would disprove Micaiah’s prophecy
He asked Ahab to stop the war
He admitted that his prophecy was uncertain
challenge.explanation: Micaiah made Ahab’s return in peace a test of whether the Lord had truly spoken through him.
challenge.q: What did Micaiah mean by saying, “If thou return at all in peace, the Lord hath not spoken by me”?

easy.explanation: The two kings went up to Ramothgilead.
easy.q: Where did Ahab and Jehoshaphat go to fight?

answers: He sent Jehoshaphat in his place
easy.explanation: Ahab said, “I will disguise myself,” and entered the battle in disguise.
easy.q: How did Ahab try to avoid being recognized in battle?

easy.explanation: The captains mistook Jehoshaphat for the king of Israel, and he cried out.
easy.q: Who cried out when the captains of the chariots pursued him?

answers: They thought he was the king of Israel
They recognized him as an ally
They wanted him to lead them
medium.explanation: They said, “Surely it is the king of Israel,” and turned to fight him.
medium.q: Why did the captains of the chariots attack Jehoshaphat?

answers: They turned back from pursuing him
medium.explanation: When they perceived that he was not the king of Israel, they turned back.
medium.q: What happened when the captains realized Jehoshaphat was not the king of Israel?

answers: He fell asleep in the evening
He returned home in the evening
medium.explanation: Ahab was wounded during the battle and died toward the end of the day.
medium.q: In the KJV, what does “died at even” mean?

answers: The captains found him in Samaria
challenge.explanation: A man drew a bow “at a venture,” and the arrow struck Ahab between the joints of his harness.
challenge.q: How was Micaiah’s prophecy fulfilled even though Ahab disguised himself?

answers: Ahab hid his identity, yet he was still wounded and killed
Ahab went alone, but Jehoshaphat won in his place
Ahab sought peace, but Syria refused
challenge.explanation: Ahab’s disguise did not prevent the foretold judgment from reaching him.
challenge.q: What contrast is shown between Ahab’s plan and its result?

answers: The dogs licked up his blood, according to the word of the Lord
The people made him king again
challenge.explanation: The KJV records that the dogs licked up his blood, fulfilling the word of the Lord.
challenge.q: Which detail at the end of the account emphasizes the shame of Ahab’s death?

easy.explanation: Jehoshaphat is called “the son of Asa.”

answers: He walked in all the ways of Ahab
He followed Asa’s way and did what was right in the eyes of the Lord
easy.explanation: He walked in all the ways of Asa and did that which was right in the eyes of the Lord.
easy.q: How does the KJV describe Jehoshaphat’s way of life?

easy.explanation: The text says, “nevertheless the high places were not taken away.”
easy.q: What remained during Jehoshaphat’s reign despite his good deeds?

answers: He drove him from the land
medium.explanation: The KJV says, “And Jehoshaphat made peace with the king of Israel.”
medium.q: What was Jehoshaphat’s relationship with the king of Israel?

answers: Build a new city in Judah
medium.explanation: He made ships to go to Ophir for gold.
medium.q: What did Jehoshaphat intend to do with the ships of Tharshish?

medium.explanation: The ships did not go to Ophir because they were broken at Eziongeber.
medium.q: What happened to Jehoshaphat’s ships at Eziongeber?

answers: His reign is presented positively, but with a noted shortcoming
challenge.explanation: He did what was right in the Lord’s eyes, yet the high places were not removed.
challenge.q: What does the combination of praise for Jehoshaphat and mention of the high places show?

challenge.explanation: Ahaziah made the offer, “But Jehoshaphat would not.”
challenge.q: What happened to Ahaziah’s offer to send servants with Jehoshaphat’s servants on the ships?

challenge.explanation: The KJV says, “and Jehoram his son reigned in his stead.”
challenge.q: Who succeeded Jehoshaphat after his death?

easy.explanation: Ahaziah is called “the son of Ahab.”
Ahaziah reigned over Israel in Samaria.
easy.q: Over which kingdom did Ahaziah reign?

easy.explanation: The text says, “For he served Baal, and worshipped him.”

answers: The way of his father, his mother, and Jeroboam the son of Nebat
The way of Asa and Jehoshaphat
The way of Micaiah and Zedekiah
medium.explanation: The KJV says he walked in the way of his father, his mother, and Jeroboam.
The text says that he reigned two years over Israel.
medium.q: How long did Ahaziah reign over Israel?

answers: He committed acts that aroused the Lord’s anger
He asked the Lord for forgiveness
medium.explanation: Serving and worshipping Baal were acts that provoked the Lord to anger.
medium.q: What does “provoked to anger the Lord God of Israel” mean here?

answers: He continued the ways of the house of Ahab and Jeroboam
He returned to the way of Asa
challenge.explanation: His conduct followed the ways of his father, his mother, and Jeroboam.
challenge.q: What connection does the account make between Ahaziah and the sins of earlier generations?

answers: His reign is presented as evil in the sight of the Lord
His reign is presented as following Jehoshaphat
His reign is presented as religiously insignificant
challenge.explanation: The account begins by saying that he did evil in the sight of the Lord and describes his Baal worship.
challenge.q: What does the description of Ahaziah’s worship of Baal show about the writer’s evaluation of his reign?

answers: He was Ahab’s son and continued his father’s ways
He was Jehoshaphat’s son and continued Asa’s way
He was Asa’s son and rejected Jeroboam’s way
challenge.explanation: Ahaziah was Ahab’s son and walked in the sinful ways associated with his family and Jeroboam.
challenge.q: What family and spiritual pattern is described in relation to Ahaziah?
